section_1.title: Prerequisites: Vectors and Determinants
section_1.content: Brief review of 2D vectors and the 2x2 determinant (ad-bc), which serves as the building block for the cross product calculation. Visualizing the area of a parallelogram.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 2x2 grid representing a 2D parallelogram spanned by vectors (a,b) and (c,d).

section_2.title: The 2D Pseudo-Cross Product
section_2.content: Explain that the cross product is strictly a 3D operation, but in 2D, we compute the 'z-component' (scalar) representing the signed area. Positive for counter-clockwise, negative for clockwise.
section_2.example: A squirrel running on a plane: the sign of the cross product tells us if the squirrel is making a left turn (+) or a right turn (-).

section_3.title: Defining the 3D Cross Product
section_3.content: Introduce the cross product result: a vector perpendicular to the original two. Define the formula using the 3x3 determinant with unit vectors i, j, k.
section_3.example: An animation of two flat rectangular plates meeting at a hinge; the cross product vector emerges from the hinge pointing along the axis of rotation.

section_4.title: Geometric Meaning: Right-Hand Rule and Magnitude
section_4.content: Explain that the magnitude |a x b| = |a||b|sin(θ), representing the area of the 3D parallelogram. Use the Right-Hand Rule to determine the direction.
section_4.example: A robotic arm joint: curling your right fingers from vector A to vector B, your thumb points in the direction of the cross product, indicating the axis of the joint's movement.

section_5.title: Summary and Application
section_5.content: Quick recap of properties (anti-commutative: a x b = -b x a) and real-world application in physics (Torque) and 3D graphics (Surface Normals).
section_5.example: A character in a video game holding a wrench; calculating the torque on a bolt using the cross product of the lever arm and the force vector.

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Review 2D vectors and area.", "2x2 determinant defines area.", "This builds the cross product."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: Vectors and Determinants", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5 + UP * 0.5, color="#FF5733")
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.5 + UP * 1.5, color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        matrix = Matrix([[r"a", r"c"], [r"b", r"d"]], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B5')

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the 3D Cross Product", [
            "3D cross product is perpendicular.",
            "Use 3x3 determinant.",
            "Result is a new vector.",
            "It defines rotation axis.",
            "Follows the hinge orientation."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        vec_a = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#33FF57")
        vec_b = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#33FF57")
        vec_c = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        
        vectors = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b, vec_c)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_a), FadeIn(vec_b), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
